messages.subject_clean: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am finding some difficulties in getting NicheMapR 1.1.4 installed in the latest R version (3.5.0). I have tried installing it in several ways (using install.packages(), with the 'tar.gz' source file, directly form github using install_github()...), but I cannot make it work. In the best case, I succeed in getting the package installed, but I am unable to load it. I get the following message:

Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘NicheMapR’:
 package ‘NicheMapR’ was installed by an R version with different internals; it needs to be reinstalled for use with this R version

It seems that the new version of R has major changes (including internal functions and so on), and is causing this behaviour. I would be really pleased if other NicheMapR users could let me know if they are experiencing the same issue. Alternatively, I would like to know the version of R with which this version of NicheMapR was compiled, to downgrade R, if necessary.

Thank you very much in advance and apologies for any inconvenience,
Urtzi

messages.subject_clean: NicheMapR 1.4 prerelease (please test it out) and a soil moisture paper
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

For those of you that may experience a similar issue, Mike found a solution.

The problem solved when I installed a compatible version of 'gfortran' (available at: https://gcc.gnu.org/wiki/GFortranBinaries#) and re-installed NicheMapR from Mike's repository on github (>devtools::install_github("mrke/NicheMapR")).

Hope this helps someone,

Best wishes,
Urtzi

messages.subject: Re: Error in library(NicheMapR) : there is no package called ‘NicheMapR’
messages.subject_clean: Error in library(NicheMapR) : there is no package called ‘NicheMapR’
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Have you tried installing NicheMapR by using devtools? If you install this you can install the latest version of the software by using:

install_github("mrke/nichemapr")

I believe Mike's 2016 paper detailing the microclimate model provides all the code to install it this way. It can be found here: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/ecog.02360

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Modelling Invertebrates
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I was wondering if anyone has any experience in using NicheMapR to model inverts (specifically insects).
Is it possible/recommended using the current ectotherm model or is there a specific invert model that should be used instead?

Many thanks
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Modelling Invertebrates
messages.body_plain: Hi Simon you can use the ectotherm model as is - just be sure to choose the appropriate local height in the microclimate model. There is a holometabolic DEB model that is now part of the ectotherm model (see recent paper with Maino as the lead author in Current Opinions in Insect Science for an e.g.).
